subsystems.name: Feedstock extraction and refining
subsystems.role: turns asteroid or lunar rock into structural metal, silicon and glass without shipping anything from Earth.

subsystems.name: Bulk launch
subsystems.role: lifts material off a low-gravity body cheaply enough to matter.

subsystems.name: Orbital printing units
subsystems.role: the actual 'printers' — autonomous machines that build structures in vacuum and microgravity.
parts: electron-beam or laser wire deposition head

subsystems.name: Power and thermal control
subsystems.role: printing and refining need continuous power and somewhere to dump heat.

subsystems.name: Assembly and station-keeping
subsystems.role: joins printed pieces and keeps the swarm from drifting apart.

subsystems.name: Autonomy and communications
subsystems.role: light-lag makes joysticks useless; the swarm must run itself.

buildSteps.title: Prospect a small body
buildSteps.detail: Survey a near-Earth asteroid or a lunar polar region by remote sensing and sampling to find accessible metal, silicon and oxygen.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate extraction
buildSteps.detail: Land a robotic plant that digs or scrapes regolith, separates useful elements and stores them as powder, wire or ingots.

buildSteps.title: Print in vacuum and microgravity
buildSteps.detail: Prove that additive manufacturing works without gravity-driven convection or an atmosphere — electron-beam wire deposition for metal, focused heat for sintering rock.

buildSteps.title: Build the launcher
buildSteps.detail: Install an electromagnetic mass driver on the low-gravity body to fling feedstock canisters into a rendezvous orbit at a fraction of rocket cost.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the first collectors
buildSteps.detail: Print thin supports and photovoltaic or mirror surfaces, fly them into a ring or shell pattern, and keep them spaced by autonomous station-keeping.

buildSteps.title: Close the replication loop
buildSteps.detail: The decisive step on paper: printers and miners that build copies of themselves from local material, so capacity grows exponentially rather than linearly.

buildSteps.title: Scale the swarm
buildSteps.detail: With doubling times of months to years, the number of units grows until intercepted starlight is a measurable fraction of the star's output.

buildSteps.title: Attempt larger shells
buildSteps.detail: Only after the swarm exists would anyone try rigid, joined structures — and even then as overlapping independent elements, not one continuous shell.

prerequisites.why: a 3D printer has operated on the ISS since 2014, but nothing has printed structural metal at tonne scale in orbit.
oxygen and water have been extracted from simulated regolith and small asteroid samples returned, but no off-Earth refinery has run continuously.
laboratory mass drivers exist; flinging payloads to orbital velocity has never been done.
self-organising robot teams are demonstrated in labs and warehouses, not as self-repairing space factories.
no machine has ever built a complete copy of itself from raw material; this is the single assumption the whole idea rests on.
kilometre-scale foils and trusses have flown, but nothing approaching the area needed for a stellar collector.

pathway.milestone: orbital 3D printing, asteroid sample returns and ISRU benchtop demonstrations
pathway.unlocks: the component technologies, none yet integrated.

pathway.milestone: a robotic pilot plant that mines, refines and prints structural parts on the Moon or an asteroid
pathway.unlocks: proof that off-Earth manufacturing can run without resupply.

pathway.milestone: a mass driver delivering bulk feedstock to a construction site in orbit
pathway.unlocks: raw material cost low enough for megastructure-scale building.

pathway.milestone: self-expanding manufacturing, where each generation of printers builds the next
pathway.unlocks: exponential growth of collector area — the theoretical engine of a Dyson swarm.

pathway.milestone: a swarm capturing a noticeable share of a star's light; any talk of a solid shell remains physically unsound because no known material could hold it and no orbit would keep it stable
pathway.unlocks: power and habitat area at a scale far beyond planetary resources.
